ip_top_stories.title: German Court Rules Suno's AI Memorized and Reproduced Copyrighted Songs
ip_top_stories.summary: A German court has ruled against Suno AI, finding that the music generator memorized and reproduced copyrighted songs in its training process. The case, brought by GEMA, marks a significant legal precedent for AI music generation and copyright liability in Europe.

ip_top_stories.title: Meta Seeks To Block Zuckerberg Depo In AI Copyright Cases
ip_top_stories.summary: Meta is seeking to block the deposition of Mark Zuckerberg in ongoing AI copyright litigation. The move signals Meta's effort to limit executive exposure as courts continue to scrutinise AI companies' training data practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic Pushes to Dismiss Copyright Lawsuit Over AI Training
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic has filed to dismiss a copyright lawsuit relating to its AI training practices. The case is part of a broader wave of litigation challenging how AI companies use copyrighted material to train large language models.

ip_top_stories.title: Why is Anthropic destroying books? | Kathryn James
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis piece examining Anthropic's reported practice of destroying physical books as part of its AI training pipeline, raising questions about copyright compliance and the legal and ethical implications for publishers and authors.

ip_top_stories.title: The Underappreciated Third U.S. Fair Use Factor in Copyright Infringement Cases Concerning AI Training
ip_top_stories.summary: A legal analysis focusing on the third fair use factor — the amount and substantiality of the portion used — as an underexamined element in AI training copyright cases. The piece argues this factor deserves greater scrutiny in current litigation involving AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Delhi HC ruling on ANI-OpenAI copyright case sparks debate over fair dealing and judicial activism
ip_further_links.summary: India's Delhi High Court ruling in the ANI-OpenAI copyright case has prompted debate about the scope of fair dealing doctrine and concerns over judicial overreach in AI-related IP disputes.

ip_further_links.title: No news content for AI-training without licences | Hindustan Times
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece arguing that news publishers should not be required to permit their content to be used for AI training without obtaining licences and appropriate compensation.

ip_further_links.title: Online Shadow Libraries And Why They're Being Implicated In AI Copyright Lawsuits
ip_further_links.summary: An explainer on how online shadow libraries — repositories of pirated books and papers — are becoming central to AI copyright litigation as evidence of training data sources.

ip_further_links.title: Nvidia faces shareholder suit over AI training and 'fraudulent scheme'
ip_further_links.summary: Nvidia is facing a shareholder lawsuit alleging a fraudulent scheme related to its AI training practices and use of copyrighted data.

ip_further_links.title: FEATURE: Japan contests rewrite rules as generative AI spreads - Japan Wire by Kyodo News
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is reviewing its copyright framework in response to the proliferation of generative AI, with debate over whether existing rules permitting broad AI training exemptions should be revised.

ip_further_links.title: Improving the legal framework to develop the publishing ecosystem in the digital environment
ip_further_links.summary: A policy-focused piece examining proposed improvements to the legal framework governing digital publishing, including issues around AI, copyright, and the broader publishing ecosystem.

ip_further_links.title: SCCA's student chapter debate spotlights AI copyright
ip_further_links.summary: A student chapter debate organised by the SCCA has drawn attention to unresolved AI copyright questions, reflecting growing engagement with IP issues in academic and legal communities.

ip_further_links.title: Spending on College Course Materials Falls Again [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: A Publishers Weekly report finds that student spending on college course materials declined again in the 2025–2026 academic year, continuing a multi-year trend with implications for academic publishers.
